title: Investigation Slab — compact metrics, trace anchors, and dashboard skeleton
content:
Goal:
Create a compact, reusable investigation "slab" — a minimal set of metrics, prebuilt queries, trace anchor rules, and a 6-panel dashboard skeleton that on-call and triage engineers can use to go from alert -> root cause in under 12 minutes for common token-serving incidents (latency spikes, token dropouts, model fallback loops, cold-cache storms).

Context / why a "slab":
- We have large, noisy dashboards; first 10 mins of an incident are spent hunting for the right query and the right trace window.
- The slab is intentionally small (6–8 signals + 2 trace anchors + 1 synthetic check) so responders get deterministic steps.
- This doc is a working template: copy into a dashboard, wire the variables (model, region, route), and iterate.

When to use this slab:
- Alert types: P95 latency >= SLO for 5m, token-serving error spike, sudden model fallback rate increase, burst in cold-cache misses.
- Not for multi-hour degradations that need long-form correlation (use full observability runway docs).

Slab components (high level):
1) Shortlist metrics (operational) — each metric includes a brief definition and a suggested query (pseudocode / PromQL-style).
2) Trace anchors — span selection heuristics and tags that matter.
3) Dashboard skeleton — 6 panels ordered for fast triage.
4) Quick-runbook snippet for first-responder actions.
5) Cost guardrails & sampling guidance.

1) Shortlist metrics (definitions + query hints):
- request_rate: request.count per minute grouped by route/model. Query hint: rate(requests_total[1m]) by (route,model_version) — use tenant filter if multi-tenant.
- p95_server_latency_ms: 95th percentile of end-to-end server latency (ingress->response). Hint: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(server_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le,route,model_version)).
- kv_cache_hit_ratio: ratio of KV hits to total token lookups. Hint: sum(kv_cache_hits)/sum(kv_cache_lookups) by (model_version). Watch for sudden drops -> cold cache.
- model_fallback_rate: count of fallback-policy triggers / total requests. Hint: rate(fallback_trigger_total[5m])/rate(requests_total[5m]).
- token_generation_errors: error count normalized by tokens generated. Hint: rate(token_errors_total[5m]) / max(rate(tokens_generated_total[5m]), 1).
- batch_size_avg: average batch size observed at runtime. Hint: avg_over_time(batch_size[5m]) by (shard).
- queue_depth: instant queue length for each shard/pool. Hint: max(queue_depth{pool=~".*"}) by (pool).
- synthetic_probe_latency: probe latency for the active probe route (1 probe every 30s).

2) Trace anchors (heuristics):
- Anchor A (user-level hotpath): pick a trace that has the alerting request_id and spans: ingress->router->model-call->kv-lookup->emit. Filter spans where span.tag.model_version == alerted_model_version and span.duration > p95. Collect these fields: span_id, trace_id, model_version, shard_id, batch_size, seq_len, token_count, host.
- Anchor B (backend systemic): pick a trace where queue_depth >= 90th pct and model_call.duration high but with kv_cache.hit==false. This helps detect cold-cache amplification.
- Sampling rules: for alerts, temporarily increase trace sampling to 100% for the affected model_version and route for 5 minutes. Otherwise keep adaptive sampling (5% overall, 20% for errors).

3) Dashboard skeleton (6 panels, ordered):
Top row (context)
- Panel 1: Incident summary + fast filters (time range, model_version, region, route).
- Panel 2: Request rate heatmap (by route/model) — shows where traffic shifted.
Middle row (triage)
- Panel 3: P95/P99 server latency timeseries + synthetic_probe latency overlay.
- Panel 4: KV cache hit ratio + cache miss spike annotation.
Bottom row (deep dive)
- Panel 5: Model fallback rate + errors stacked by cause (timeout, mem OOM, mismatch).
- Panel 6: Representative trace list (top 10 traces by duration) with direct link to trace viewer and prefilled trace anchors (Anchor A/B).

Layout notes: emphasize compact width (two columns). Each panel includes a small query inspector button that copies the query. Default time window: last 30m, lookback steps: 1m.

4) Quick-runbook (first-responder):
0) Open slab dashboard -> confirm alert window and affected model_version.
1) Check Panel 2 & 3: is traffic spike present? If yes, check batching: Panel 4 shows avg batch_size; if batch_size decreased while qDepth increased -> starvation.
2) Check KV cache hits (Panel 4): drop -> likely cold-cache or eviction policy change. If cache drop coincides with new model_version rollout, tag rollback candidate.
3) Check model_fallback_rate (Panel 5): if fallback rising -> inspect model-serving logs for OOM/timeouts (link to PR /k8s events). If fallback triggers are > 5% of requests, flip to fallback SLO and open escalation.
4) Pick top trace from Panel 6 -> follow Anchor A for contextual spans. Note span attributes (shard, host, batch_size) and correlate to infra metrics (GPU load, mem) — link to infra console.
5) If no smoking gun in 15m: enable higher sampling on the model_version and create an Investigation Slack thread with trace links and query snapshots.

5) Sampling & cost guardrails:
- Default: keep sampling at 5% global, errors 20%, but auto-sample 100% for any model_version that has an active incident for 5m.
- Trace retention: keep incident-sampled traces for 14 days, aggregated trace metrics for 90 days. Be mindful of trace link churn (high-card spans like prompt hashes should be redacted).
- Cost note: enabling 100% sampling for heavy traffic models (>= 1k rpm) will multiply trace storage — add an alert to oncall costs channel if cumulative trace bytes > X in 1h.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide standard binning for queue_depth panels (per-pool vs per-shard) — currently tuned per-service; need a short RFC.
- Add a small set of canned alerts that map directly to slab steps (e.g., cache-drop -> prefill rollback play).
- Create a templated dashboard JSON export + dashboard-creation script for infra-as-code.

Notes to self / shorthand:
- keep panel queries parameterized with $model_version, $route, $tenant for easy cloning.
- Flag every slab-created dashboard with tag: "slab:investigation" in dashboard metadata.
- Crosslink to runbook page: CONFLUENCE-OBS/Investigation-Slab (TODO: create).

Appendix: quick example PromQL snippets (pseudocode)
- p95_server_latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(server_latency_bucket{route="$route", model_version="$model_version"}[5m])) by (le))
- kv_cache_hit_ratio: sum(rate(kv_cache_hit_total{model_version="$model_version"}[5m])) / max(sum(rate(kv_cache_lookup_total{model_version="$model_version"}[5m])), 1)
- model_fallback_rate: sum(rate(fallback_trigger_total{route="$route"}[5m])) / max(sum(rate(requests_total{route="$route"}[5m])), 1)

If this slab looks useful, next steps:
- (short) convert to dashboard template and push into dashboard repo as /dashboards/slabs/investigation-slab.json
- (medium) land auto-sampling toggle in trace-service that responds to incident tags
- (long) formalize slab onboarding in oncall playbook and include a 10-min hands-on lab in SRE bootcamp.

---
Working draft — feedback welcome.
